inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 Net Profit used as distributable earnings proxy and mid-cycle normalization anchor. Flow Traders has no traditional FCF — trading capital IS the productive asset. Q1-2026 net profit of EUR 50.4m (annualised ~EUR 201m) is NOT used as the anchor to avoid peak-volatility extrapolation. FY2025 at EUR 133.6m reflects a healthy but not exceptional mid-cycle year.
inputs.trading_capital_note: Record high EUR 1,092m at end Q1-2026 (up 36% YoY), including $200m private credit facility drawn October 2025.
inputs.debt_note: $200m private credit facility (SOFR+5%, 6-year term, drawn October 2025) ~EUR 186m. Cash EUR 8m per Q1-2026 balance sheet. Annualised interest expense ~EUR 18-19m.

historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: 3-year equity CAGR (FY2022-FY2025, +12.7%) is the primary anchor. The 5-year NTI and EPS CAGRs are negative because FY2020 was an anomalous COVID-volatility year (NTI EUR 933m vs EUR 300-486m in normal years). Equity CAGR is the most reliable metric as it reflects book value compounding through retained earnings. The pre-COVID 6-year NTI CAGR (FY2019-FY2025) of 14.4% confirms mid-teens structural growth is achievable in the bull case. Updated equity CAGR including Q1-2026 equity of EUR 918.4m over 3.25 years is 13.6%, confirming the trend.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 5-year NTI and EPS CAGRs are negative due to the anomalous FY2020 COVID volatility base (NTI EUR 933m). The equity 5yr CAGR of 8.0% diverges from NTI/EPS 5yr by more than 30pp, but this is entirely COVID-base distortion, not a structural divergence. Flagged for transparency; not a valuation concern.
historical_growth.cyclicality_note: Flow Traders earnings are highly cyclical: FY2020 NTI EUR 933m (COVID peak), FY2021 EUR 384m, FY2022 EUR 460m, FY2023 (low vol) EUR 300m, FY2024 EUR 468m, FY2025 EUR 486m, Q1-2026 NTI EUR 155.9m (strong quarter). Mid-cycle NP average FY2021-FY2025 is EUR 114m. FY2025 NP of EUR 133.6m is used as anchor — above mid-cycle average but below annualised Q1-2026 run-rate to avoid peak extrapolation. All scenarios anchored to normalized earnings, not peak or trough.

base.description: Moderate market conditions with normal volatility (VIX ~17-20). Capital expansion delivers incremental NTI. Fixed costs rise per FY2026 updated guidance (EUR 235-245m). Asia and digital assets grow steadily. Interest expense ~EUR 18-19m annualised weighs on net profit. Net profit grows at moderate rates from FY2025 mid-cycle anchor, decelerating toward maturity.
base.wacc_rationale: 11% reflects: risk-free rate ~3.5% (German 10yr Bund), equity risk premium 5.5%, beta ~1.3 for cyclical earnings, small-cap Euronext premium 0.5%. Higher than typical US comps to reflect earnings volatility, vol-dependency, and leverage from $200m PCF.

bull.description: Elevated market volatility (VIX 20+), strong capital deployment benefits, Asia expansion materially exceeds expectations, digital assets and tokenization accelerate per Horizon 2030 roadmap. Trading capital fully deployed generating high incremental NTI. EUR 140m base reflects Q1-2026 momentum and expanded capital benefits.
bull.wacc_rationale: 10% in bull case as structural tailwinds reduce cyclical risk perception, elevated volatility regime demonstrates sustainable earnings power, and PCF is fully and efficiently deployed.

bear.description: Prolonged low-volatility environment (VIX 12-14) similar to FY2023 trough. Fixed opex guidance creep at EUR 235-245m and EUR 18-19m interest burden creates structural earnings compression. Competitive pressure from Citadel and Jane Street intensifies. Americas market remains impenetrable at scale. Stressed EUR 100m base reflects below-mid-cycle conditions consistent with FY2023 NP trajectory.
bear.wacc_rationale: 13% in bear case reflects materialized cyclical risk, higher leverage concern, elevated fixed cost base, and investor flight from volatile-earnings businesses in a sustained low-vol regime.

base.note: At EUR 25.58, the stock trades approximately 10.6% below the base-case 15%-CAGR entry price of EUR 28.61. This implies a modest margin of safety exists in the base case — the stock is slightly cheaper than the threshold needed to earn 15% annualised to intrinsic value.

bull.note: Stock trades 49.5% below bull-case 15%-CAGR entry price — represents a deeply discounted entry relative to the bull case terminal value.

bear.note: Current price is 125% above the bear-case 15%-CAGR entry price, reflecting the downside risk of a prolonged low-volatility environment.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = WACC 9% to 13% (top to bottom). Columns = Terminal Growth 2.0% to 4.0% (left to right). Base inputs: FY2025 Net Profit EUR 133.6m, growth rates Y1-Y5: 10/9/8/7/6%. Current price EUR 25.58 sits inside the WACC 12-13% rows — the market is implicitly pricing in either high risk or low long-term growth. All values in EUR per share.

probability_weighted.rationale: Base 50%: most likely outcome reflecting continued mid-cycle market conditions (VIX ~18) and incremental capital deployment benefits from expanded trading capital. Bull 25%: elevated volatility regime with Asia and digital assets exceeding expectations, Horizon 2030 on track. Bear 25%: prolonged low-vol period materializes (VIX 12-14 as seen post-Q2-2026 pre-close), competitive pressure intensifies, fixed opex creep compounds.

sanity_check.verdict: The base IV of EUR 44.38 implies 14.5x FY2025 EPS at the implied price — at the upper end of the historical 5-12x range. However, this is applied to FY2025 (a mid-cycle year) and the terminal-year implied P/E is only 9.9x — a reasonable and conservative exit multiple for a sustained business. The EV/NTI of 4.38x at base IV is elevated versus Flow Traders' typical 1.5-3.0x historical EV/NTI; this reflects the terminal-value-heavy nature of DCF on a business with rising retained equity. No auto-fix applied: the growth rates (10/9/8/7/6%) are anchored to mid-cycle FY2025 NP of EUR 133.6m, NOT to Q1-2026 annualised run-rate of EUR 201m+, and the WACC of 11% is already elevated vs peers to reflect cyclicality. The bear case IV of EUR 16.72 and bear P/B of 0.80x provides a credible downside anchor. EV/NTI would be unrealistic IF applied to peak-Q1-2026-annualised earnings — but it is not.
sanity_check.peak_earnings_check: Q1-2026 annualised NTI = EUR 624m. Base Y5 NTI implied at 27% net margin = EUR 713m. This is 1.5x FY2025 NTI, which requires sustained above-average market conditions. The bull case Y5 NP of EUR 281m implies NTI of ~EUR 1,021m — directly in line with Horizon 2030 NTI >EUR 1bn target. No scenario extrapolates peak COVID or Q1-2026-type volatility across the full horizon.

valuation_context.commentary: At EUR 25.58, Flow Traders trades at 8.3x FY2025 earnings and 1.22x Q1-2026 book value — a meaningful discount versus US market-making peer Virtu Financial (approximately 12-14x earnings). The sensitivity matrix shows base-case intrinsic value ranges from EUR 32-72 across all reasonable WACC (9-13%) and terminal growth (2-4%) assumptions. The stock is trading below the base-case 15%-CAGR entry price of EUR 28.61, implying modest undervaluation on mid-cycle normalized assumptions. Key overhangs suppressing the multiple: (1) extreme earnings cyclicality tied to VIX — Q2-2026 pre-close signals muted quarter; (2) dividend and buyback suspended through at least 2030; (3) EUR 178m net debt adding leverage risk; (4) fixed opex guidance raised twice in two months to EUR 235-245m, undermining confidence in cost discipline. A re-rating catalyst would require either dividend resumption, demonstrated ROI on trading capital expansion, or a sustained elevated-volatility regime that proves the EUR 1bn NTI Horizon 2030 target is achievable.

valuation_philosophy: Flow Traders is a market-making firm with NO recurring revenue, NO client AuM, and earnings that can swing 30-50% within a single quarter based purely on market volatility. Standard DCF methodology is applied but with the following disciplined constraints: (1) Earnings anchor is FY2025 net profit of EUR 133.6m — a mid-cycle year that is above the EUR 114m FY2021-FY2025 average but well below both the FY2020 COVID peak (EUR 465m) and the Q1-2026 annualised run-rate (EUR ~200m+); (2) WACC is set at 11-13% across scenarios, materially above the 8-10% used for stable businesses, to compensate for earnings unpredictability; (3) Terminal growth of 2-3.5% reflects the structural ETP industry tailwind but not a perpetuation of peak-vol conditions; (4) The bear case (EUR 16.72, -34.6% from current) is explicitly modelled on FY2023-like NTI conditions with a rising fixed cost base — this is a fully plausible near-term outcome if VIX remains suppressed. Investors should treat the base IV of EUR 44.38 as a mid-cycle fair value, not a near-term price target, and must be comfortable owning through periods where the stock may trade at or below the bear-case IV.
